claims.text: The starting material is additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 with an fcc matrix.
The starting material is homogenized and has a uniform elemental distribution.
The starting material has minimal surface oxide.
Elevated-temperature degradation is governed by a dynamic layered oxide scale whose evolution depends on the gas environment.
In an oxidizing atmosphere, rapid initial oxidation of Ni creates a Ni-enriched pre-oxide.
The Ni-enriched pre-oxide promotes selective oxidation of Cr into a Cr2O3 barrier layer.
The Cr2O3 layer retards subsequent oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Retarded oxygen diffusion maintains the fcc matrix and preserves strength and fatigue performance.
The layered scale has an outer mixed oxide containing Fe, Co, and contributions from Ti.
Under reducing conditions, insufficient Cr oxidation prevents formation of a coherent protective barrier.
Reducing conditions produce a more porous and less adherent oxide film.
The absence of a coherent barrier under reducing conditions accelerates internal oxidation and elemental redistribution.
Oxidizing exposure will produce a stable, thin layered scale with limited overall thickness.
The scale formed under reducing exposure will be thicker and less coherent than the scale formed under oxidizing exposure.
Reducing exposure will cause a greater loss of fatigue strength and other mechanical properties than oxidizing exposure.
The as-built alloy has high strength and fatigue performance.
The proposed mechanism applies from about 400 to 600 degrees Celsius under approximately 10 mbar oxygen or hydrogen-rich reducing gas.
Limiting exposures to a few minutes through a few hours avoids overlapping phase transformations.
Exact oxide-thickness differences, segregation rates, and Ti contributions are uncertain and may vary with processing and gas composition.

Failure to observe a Cr-rich layered scale and correspondingly lower degradation under oxidizing exposure, or observation of similar degradation in both gases, would falsify the proposed gas-dependent mechanism.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as homogenized in one field but as as-built in another; these are distinct processing states unless the baseline is explicitly defined as the pre-homogenization condition.
